findings.sourceReading: Virgilia recalls that Beatrice repeatedly and emphatically boasted of surpassing her master.
findings.alternative: Her boasts may have sounded harsh or disrespectful toward her master. The adverb emphasizes how much she boasted, which matters to Virgilia’s teasing reminder.

findings.sourceReading: Eva’s inner voice taunts her to give up, resign, and simply go to sleep under a futon if she is that tired.
findings.alternative: “Forever” can heighten the cruel, dreamlike self-taunt without literally asserting death. It adds a materially darker finality absent from the line.

MG.translation: Am I touching the door with both hands, with the book...no, the door right there in front of me, ready to be opened, ...and yet still unable to reach the other side?

findings.sourceReading: Eva imagines herself with both hands on the door and already opening it, yet still unable to cross to the Golden Land beyond.
findings.alternative: A door poised to open preserves her position at the threshold. It changes the explicit paradox from having opened the door without reaching the far side to merely not having opened it yet.

findings.description: Both editions’ “infantile” wording follows the original-PC 低脳な, describing a low-intelligence or stupid riddle.
